def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (T : ℕ) (N : S1 Bool Bool), N.D9 → S1.D5 T N d15 → T ≤ N.d13
a_raw: {"translation": "Target names (without asserting or proving) the following proposition: for every natural number T and every system N of type S1 Bool Bool, if N satisfies the acyclicity condition D9 and agrees with the reference system d15 on all boolean input lists of length at most T (condition D5), then T is less than or equal to the cardinality of N's index type A1. In full detail: a system N of type S1 Bool Bool consists of a finite type A1 of indices (whose number of elements is N.d13), a family of types A3 n indexed by n in A1 (which need not be finite and may depend on n), an initial global state a4 assigning an element of A3 n to each n in A1, an update function a5 taking an index n, a global state σ : (m : A1) → A3 m, and an input x : Bool to a value in A3 n, and an output function a6 mapping global states to Bool. On a finite list xs of booleans, N computes its output by starting at a4, repeatedly applying the synchronous update (fun σ x => fun n => N.a5 n σ x) left-to-right for each element of xs, and finally applying a6. Hypothesis 1 (N.D9) says that the semantic dependency graph on A1 is acyclic: writing an edge from m to n (N.D8 m n) whenever there exist two global states σ, σ' (not required to be reachable from a4) that agree on all k ≠ m and a boolean input x such that N.a5 n σ x ≠ N.a5 n σ' x, there is no index n in A1 with a nonempty directed path (one or more edges) from n to n (so neither self-loops nor longer directed cycles exist; no dependency condition is imposed on a6). Hypothesis 2 (S1.D5 T N d15) says that for every list xs : List Bool with xs.length ≤ T, N produces the same boolean output as d15, where d15 is the single-index (Unit) system with Bool state, initial value false, update rule (current state || x), and output equal to its state—so d15 outputs true if xs contains at least one true and false otherwise (agreement on lists longer than T is not required). The conclusion asserts that T ≤ Fintype.card N.A1."}
translation: Target names (without asserting or proving) the following proposition: for every natural number T and every system N of type S1 Bool Bool, if N satisfies the acyclicity condition D9 and agrees with the reference system d15 on all boolean input lists of length at most T (condition D5), then T is less than or equal to the cardinality of N's index type A1. In full detail: a system N of type S1 Bool Bool consists of a finite type A1 of indices (whose number of elements is N.d13), a family of types A3 n indexed by n in A1 (which need not be finite and may depend on n), an initial global state a4 assigning an element of A3 n to each n in A1, an update function a5 taking an index n, a global state σ : (m : A1) → A3 m, and an input x : Bool to a value in A3 n, and an output function a6 mapping global states to Bool. On a finite list xs of booleans, N computes its output by starting at a4, repeatedly applying the synchronous update (fun σ x => fun n => N.a5 n σ x) left-to-right for each element of xs, and finally applying a6. Hypothesis 1 (N.D9) says that the semantic dependency graph on A1 is acyclic: writing an edge from m to n (N.D8 m n) whenever there exist two global states σ, σ' (not required to be reachable from a4) that agree on all k ≠ m and a boolean input x such that N.a5 n σ x ≠ N.a5 n σ' x, there is no index n in A1 with a nonempty directed path (one or more edges) from n to n (so neither self-loops nor longer directed cycles exist; no dependency condition is imposed on a6). Hypothesis 2 (S1.D5 T N d15) says that for every list xs : List Bool with xs.length ≤ T, N produces the same boolean output as d15, where d15 is the single-index (Unit) system with Bool state, initial value false, update rule (current state || x), and output equal to its state—so d15 outputs true if xs contains at least one true and false otherwise (agreement on lists longer than T is not required). The conclusion asserts that T ≤ Fintype.card N.A1.

divergences.description: The description says the lower bound applies to 'any feedforward (loop-free) system ... however it is built', whereas the Lean formalization quantifies over S1 Bool Bool: deterministic, discrete-time, synchronous, time-invariant sequential systems with finitely many units that receive one Bool input per timestep and update all units simultaneously with a unit (one-step) delay per dependency edge. This idealization rules out architectures outside S1—such as batch/combinational feedforward networks taking all T inputs at once, external input history buffers, or multi-step transmission delays between units—even though within S1 the per-unit state types (A3), update functions (a5), and readout (a6) are completely unrestricted.

Loop-freeness (N.D9) is defined via semantic dependency (N.D7) quantified over all global states N.D1 rather than only states reachable from the initial state a4, so a system that has a cyclic dependency only on unreachable states is excluded by the hypothesis.

When summarizing P-D54 as saying feedforward networks 'require many more neurons', the description omits P-D54's qualifier 'In general' and its explicit concession '(but not always: for instance image recognition is more efficiently implemented in feedforward convolutional networks)'. Similarly, in P-H10, the 'requires copying the network 100 times' example is given specifically while presenting Usher's objection to unrolled networks (though the authors themselves state earlier in the passage that unrolling copies the whole network for each timestep).

judgement.summary: The Lean Target faithfully formalizes the author's described lower bound—every acyclic S1 Bool Bool system agreeing with the one-unit boolean OR-latch d15 on all input sequences of length at most T has at least T units—and the description accurately characterizes the passages as stating no lower bound, with only minor caveats regarding the synchronous unit-delay sequential idealization built into S1/D9 and the omission of P-D54's 'in general / not always' concession.
